dedupe_keys.name: veragrid formerly gridcal power systems planning and simulation software

description: VeraGrid, previously named GridCal, is an open-source power systems planning and simulation program with a programming library and a graphical interface. It was started in 2015 by Santiago Peñate Vera and is developed with many contributors, with the aim of offering commercial-grade analysis free to professionals, researchers, teachers and students. The README lists linear and non-linear optimisation, RMS and electromagnetic transient simulation, short circuit, stochastic analysis, cascading blackout and investment evaluation. It is split into VeraGridEngine for data and calculations, VeraGridServer for a REST API, and the VeraGrid graphical interface. Version 6.7.0 of September 2026 added FMI 1 import and export and FMI 3 co-simulation export, underground cable models, IEEE 13-bus unbalanced feeder benchmarks, net transfer capacity contingency reports and JAO Core topology data. Coverage is not tied to a place. The software is Python, accessible on GitHub and downloadable from Zenodo releases under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 at no cost, with 39 tags. Caveats: the rename from GridCal means older papers and packages use the old name. Simulation uses are power flow, contingency and cascading failure analysis and grid expansion planning. Related records: model-pandapower and platform-powsybl are comparable open tools.
